subject: medicine
title: Aplastic Anaemia and Bone Marrow Failure

steps.tx: Profound peripheral pancytopenia arising from immune-mediated destruction of multipotent haematopoietic stem cells defines acquired bone marrow failure. In **aplastic anaemia**, autoreactive cytotoxic CD8 T cells secrete interferon-gamma and tumour necrosis factor-alpha, upregulating Fas receptors on CD34+ stem cells and triggering apoptotic death. Patients present insidiously with mucosal haemorrhage and petechiae from thrombocytopenia, severe fatigue from anaemia, and recurrent bacterial or fungal infections from neutropenia. Splenomegaly and lymphadenopathy are characteristically absent, and their presence strongly suggests an alternative malignant or infiltrative etiology.
steps.say: Profound peripheral pancytopenia arising from immune-mediated destruction of multipotent haematopoietic stem cells defines acquired bone marrow failure. In aplastic anaemia, autoreactive cytotoxic CD8 T cells secrete interferon-gamma and tumour necrosis factor, triggering stem cell apoptotic death. Patients present with mucosal bleeding from thrombocytopenia, fatigue from anaemia, and recurrent infections from neutropenia. Splenomegaly and lymphadenopathy are characteristically absent, and their presence suggests an alternative diagnosis.

steps.tx: Performing a trephine bone marrow biopsy provides the definitive diagnostic confirmation of aplastic anaemia. Histopathological evaluation reveals profound **hypocellular marrow** with extensive replacement of haematopoietic elements by empty adipose tissue and loose stroma. Severe aplastic anaemia is defined by marrow cellularity below twenty-five percent alongside at least two of the following peripheral blood criteria: absolute neutrophil count under 500 per microlitre, platelet count under 20,000 per microlitre, and absolute reticulocyte count under 20,000 per microlitre (or corrected reticulocyte count under one percent).
steps.say: Performing a trephine bone marrow biopsy provides the definitive diagnostic confirmation of aplastic anaemia. Histopathological evaluation reveals profound hypocellular marrow with extensive replacement of haematopoietic elements by empty adipose tissue and loose stroma. Severe aplastic anaemia is defined by marrow cellularity below twenty-five percent alongside severe neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, or absolute reticulocytopenia on peripheral blood analysis.

steps.tx: Definitive first-line therapy for severe aplastic anaemia depends upon patient age and the availability of a human leukocyte antigen (HLA) matched sibling donor. In young patients under forty years with a matched sibling, allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation represents the curative gold standard. In older patients or those lacking an HLA-matched sibling, intensive immunosuppressive therapy combining horse **antithymocyte globulin** (ATG) and oral cyclosporine achieves haematological response in over sixty to seventy percent of cases. Co-administering the thrombopoietin receptor agonist eltrombopag significantly accelerates trilineage haematopoietic recovery.
steps.say: Definitive first-line therapy for severe aplastic anaemia depends upon patient age and the availability of a matched sibling donor. In young patients with a matched sibling, allogeneic stem cell transplantation represents the curative gold standard. In older individuals or those without a sibling donor, immunosuppressive therapy combining antithymocyte globulin and cyclosporine achieves haematological response in most cases. Adding the thrombopoietin agonist eltrombopag accelerates trilineage recovery.

steps.tx: Inherited DNA repair defects cause constitutional aplastic anaemia characterized by physical malformations and pronounced chromosomal instability. In **fanconi anaemia**, autosomal recessive mutations in the FANC gene complex impair homologous recombination repair of DNA interstrand cross-links. Children present between five and ten years of age with progressive bone marrow failure, short stature, microcephaly, café-au-lait spots, and absent or hypoplastic thumbs and radii. Exposing peripheral blood lymphocytes to diepoxybutane (DEB) or mitomycin C induces extensive chromosomal breakage, establishing the definitive laboratory diagnosis and signaling heightened leukaemia risk.
steps.say: Inherited DNA repair defects cause constitutional aplastic anaemia characterized by physical malformations and chromosomal instability. In fanconi anaemia, autosomal recessive mutations impair homologous recombination repair of DNA cross-links. Children present between five and ten years of age with progressive bone marrow failure, short stature, café-au-lait spots, and absent or hypoplastic thumbs. Exposing lymphocytes to diepoxybutane induces chromosomal breakage, confirming the diagnosis.

left.title: Fanconi Anaemia
points: Defect in DNA interstrand cross-link repair
Radial ray and thumb anomalies, short stature
Chromosomal breakage test with DEB positive

steps.tx: Selective autoimmune or infectious suppression of erythroid progenitors producing severe isolated normocytic or macrocytic anaemia defines **pure red cell aplasia**. Bone marrow examination demonstrates a virtual absence of erythroblasts (< 1%) with completely preserved granulocytic and megakaryocytic lineages. Acquired PRCA strongly associates with benign thymoma, requiring routine contrast-enhanced chest CT imaging. Furthermore, infection with human parvovirus B19 selectively invades and lyses erythroid precursors via the erythrocyte P antigen, precipitating acute transient aplastic crises in patients with pre-existing haemolytic anaemias.
steps.say: Selective autoimmune or infectious suppression of erythroid progenitors producing severe isolated anaemia defines pure red cell aplasia. Bone marrow examination demonstrates a virtual absence of erythroblasts with preserved granulocyte and platelet precursors. Acquired pure red cell aplasia associates strongly with benign thymoma, requiring chest imaging. Furthermore, infection with human parvovirus B19 selectively lyses erythroid progenitors via the P antigen, causing transient aplastic crises in haemolytic states.

Diagnostic Screening: Chest CT for Thymoma & Parvovirus PCR

steps.tx: Clonal haematopoietic stem cell disorders characterized by ineffective haematopoiesis, peripheral cytopenias, and a high propensity for transformation into acute myeloid leukaemia define **myelodysplastic syndrome** (MDS). Striking predominantly older adults over sixty-five years, bone marrow examination characteristically reveals hypercellular or normocellular marrow with prominent morphological dysplasia across one or more cell lineages. Characteristic cytological hallmarks on peripheral smear and aspirate include dysplastic hypogranular neutrophils with pseudo-Pelger-Huet nuclear anomaly (bilobed dumbbell nuclei), micromegakaryocytes, and ring sideroblasts.
steps.say: Clonal haematopoietic stem cell disorders characterized by ineffective haematopoiesis, peripheral cytopenias, and a high risk of transformation into acute myeloid leukaemia define myelodysplastic syndrome. Striking predominantly older adults, bone marrow examination reveals normocellular or hypercellular marrow with prominent dysplasia across cell lineages. Cytological hallmarks on peripheral blood film include hypogranular neutrophils with pseudo-Pelger-Huet bilobed nuclei and micromegakaryocytes.

rows: Bilobed dumbbell nuclei with coarse chromatin

steps.tx: A specific favourable cytogenetic subtype of myelodysplastic syndrome occurs predominantly in elderly females presenting with refractory macrocytic anaemia and thrombocytosis. Designated as the **5q- deletion syndrome**, interstitial deletion of chromosome 5q31-33 results in haploinsufficiency of the ribosomal gene RPS14 and microRNA miR-145/146a. Bone marrow examination characteristically demonstrates hypolobated, non-lobated micromegakaryocytes. Administering oral lenalidomide promotes selective ubiquitination and degradation of casein kinase 1A1, inducing durable cytogenetic remissions, transfusion independence, and normalisation of peripheral blood counts in over sixty percent of patients.
steps.say: A specific favourable subtype of myelodysplastic syndrome occurs predominantly in elderly females presenting with refractory macrocytic anaemia and elevated platelet counts. Designated as the 5q- deletion syndrome, interstitial deletion of chromosome 5q results in haploinsufficiency of ribosomal and regulatory genes. Bone marrow examination demonstrates characteristic hypolobated micromegakaryocytes. Administering oral lenalidomide induces durable cytogenetic remissions and transfusion independence in most patients.

left.title: Isolated 5q- Deletion Syndrome
points: Refractory macrocytic anaemia with normal/high platelets
Low risk of transformation to AML (< 10%)

right.title: High-Risk Myelodysplasia (Excess Blasts)
points: Rapid progression to Acute Myeloid Leukaemia
IPSS-R score: High / Very High risk

steps.tx: Risk stratification in myelodysplastic syndromes guides the clinical decision between supportive therapies, disease-modifying epigenetic agents, and allogeneic transplantation. The Revised International Prognostic Scoring System (IPSS-R) integrates cytogenetic categories, marrow blast percentage, and depth of cytopenias into five risk categories. For patients with higher-risk MDS or excess blasts, hypomethylating epigenetic agents like **azacitidine** and decitabine inhibit DNA methyltransferases, reversing aberrant gene promoter hypermethylation, restoring tumor suppressor expression, prolonging overall survival, and delaying leukaemic transformation.
steps.say: Risk stratification in myelodysplastic syndromes guides the clinical decision between supportive care, epigenetic therapy, and allogeneic stem cell transplantation. The Revised International Prognostic Scoring System integrates cytogenetic categories, marrow blast percentage, and depth of cytopenias into validated risk tiers. For patients with higher-risk disease or excess blasts, hypomethylating agents like azacitidine inhibit DNA methyltransferases, prolonging overall survival and delaying leukaemic transformation.
